fullPassage: A person who always tries to prevent harm but never does, is not generally thought of as morally good. A morally good person is one who does morally bad actions significantly less often than most and does morally good ones significantly more often than most. In judging a person not only her actions but also her intentions and motives are relevant. A morally good person must intend to do morally good actions and intend to avoid morally bad ones. A person who unintentionally prevents harm to others and does not harm them simply because things do not turn out as she intends is not morally good. Although this kind of situation generally occurs only in slapstick movies, it is worth mentioning to avoid the false impression that it is the actual consequences of a person's actions that count toward her being judged morally good or bad. But actual consequences are important. Of such a person, it may be said that she means well; but, contrary to Kant, some results are necessary before she is regarded as morally good.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 count의 (A)와 (B)에서의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: count: (A) 중요하다, 작용하다 (B) (수를) 세다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 실제 결과가 판단에 '중요하게 작용하다'(count), (B) 사과의 수를 하나씩 '세다'(count) ←정답
❌ ① (A) 세다는 결과가 판단에 작용한다는 문맥과 안 맞음
❌ ② (B) 포함하다는 사과를 세는 문맥과 다름
❌ ④ (A) 의지하다는 count on의 의미로 여기 문맥과 다름
det.tip: count 다의어: ① 중요하다/작용하다(that count toward) ② (수를) 세다(count the apples)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a reason or purpose that causes a person to act in a certain way"

det.korean: reward=보상 / motive=동기 / warning=경고 / habit=습관
det.analysis:
✅ ② motive: 사람이 특정 방식으로 행동하게 만드는 이유나 목적 → 동기(motive) ←정답
❌ ① reward: 보상 — 행동의 대가이지 이유가 아님
❌ ③ warning: 경고 — 정의와 무관
❌ ④ habit: 습관 — 반복 행동이지 행동의 이유가 아님
det.tip: a reason or purpose to act = 행동의 이유/목적 → motive(동기). 본문 intentions and motives 참고

questions.passage: In __________ (judge) a person not only her actions but also her intentions and motives are relevant. A morally good person must intend to do morally good actions and intend to avoid morally bad ones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: judge(동사: 판단하다) → judging(동명사: 판단하는 것). 전치사 In 뒤에는 동명사가 온다.
det.analysis: judge를 동명사 judging으로 변환. 전치사 In 뒤에는 명사 역할을 하는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. In judging a person = '사람을 판단할 때'.
det.tip: 전치사(In) + 동명사(-ing): judge → judging

questions.passage: But actual consequences are important. Of such a person, it may be said that she means well; but, contrary to Kant, some results are necessary before she is __________ (regard) as morally good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: regard(동사: 여기다) → regarded(과거분사). be regarded as ~ 수동태 구문에서 과거분사가 필요하다.
det.analysis: regard를 과거분사 regarded로 변환. 'she is ___ as morally good'은 be동사(is) 뒤에 과거분사가 오는 수동태(be regarded as). she is regarded as morally good = '그녀가 도덕적으로 선하다고 여겨지다'.
det.tip: be동사 + 과거분사(수동태): is regarded as → regarded

questions.passage: A person who always tries to prevent harm but never does, is not generally thought of as morally good. A morally good person is one who does morally bad actions significantly less often than most and does morally good ones significantly more often than most. In judging a person not only her actions but also her __________ are relevant. A morally good person must intend to do morally good actions and intend to avoid morally bad ones. A person who unintentionally prevents harm to others and does not harm them simply because things do not turn out as she intends is not morally good. Although this kind of situation generally occurs only in slapstick movies, it is worth mentioning to avoid the false impression that it is the actual consequences of a person's actions that count toward her being judged morally good or bad. But actual consequences are important. Of such a person, it may be said that she means well; but, contrary to Kant, some results are necessary before she is regarded as morally good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: intentions and motives=의도와 동기 / friends and family=친구와 가족 / words and promises=말과 약속 / fears and doubts=두려움과 의심
det.analysis:
✅ ① intentions and motives: 사람을 판단할 때 행동뿐 아니라 '의도와 동기'도 관련 있다 ←정답
❌ ② friends and family: 친구와 가족 — 도덕적 판단 기준과 무관
❌ ③ words and promises: 말과 약속 — 본문 논지와 다름
❌ ④ fears and doubts: 두려움과 의심 — 문맥 부적절
det.tip: not only her actions but also her ___ are relevant → 행동과 대비되는 '의도와 동기'

questions.passage: A person who always tries to prevent harm but never does, is not generally thought of as morally good. A morally good person is one who does morally bad actions significantly less often than most and does morally good ones significantly more often than most. In judging a person not only her actions but also her intentions and motives are relevant. A morally good person must intend to do morally good actions and intend to avoid morally bad ones. A person who unintentionally prevents harm to others and does not harm them simply because things do not turn out as she intends is not morally good. Although this kind of situation generally occurs only in slapstick movies, it is worth mentioning to avoid the false impression that it is the actual consequences of a person's actions that count toward her being judged morally good or bad. But actual consequences are important. Of such a person, it may be said that she __________; but, contrary to Kant, some results are necessary before she is regarded as morally good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: works hard=열심히 일하다 / feels sorry=미안해하다 / gives up=포기하다 / means well=선의를 갖다
det.analysis:
✅ ④ means well: 그런 사람에 대해 '선의를 갖고 있다'고 말할 수 있지만, 결과가 있어야 도덕적으로 선하다고 여겨진다는 대조 흐름 ←정답
❌ ① works hard: 열심히 일하다 — 의도(선의)와 결과의 대비와 다름
❌ ② feels sorry: 미안해하다 — 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ gives up: 포기하다 — 문맥 부적절
det.tip: it may be said that she ___; but ... some results are necessary → 선의는 있으나(means well) 결과 필요
